encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with concern that abdomen seems larger than expected for gestational age and shortness of breath for the past week

lines: Routine prenatal visit with concern that abdomen seems larger than expected for gestational age and shortness of breath for the past week
The pregnancy has been uneventful until now.
However, she has noticed that her abdomen seems larger than expected for her gestational age and has been experiencing shortness of breath for the past week.
She reports no personal medical history.
Her first child is healthy with no medical issues.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
Blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
The uterus is larger than expected for gestational age, and there is a notable absence of fetal heart sounds.
The obstetrician orders a complete blood count and hemoglobin electrophoresis.

The laboratory results are as follows: - Hemoglobin: 11 g/dL (Normal: 11-14 g/dL) - Hematocrit: 33% (Normal: 34-40%) - MCV: 70 fL (Normal: 80-100 fL) - Hemoglobin electrophoresis: HbA 97%, HbA2 2.5%, HbF 0.5%, Hb Barts (γ4) 10%
An ultrasound reveals polyhydramnios, placental thickening, and fetal ascites.
A Doppler study shows increased peak systolic velocity in the middle cerebral artery.

encounters.cc: Routine prenatal visit with history of resolved cold-like illness two weeks ago

lines: Routine prenatal visit with history of resolved cold-like illness two weeks ago
The patient is a 28-year-old female with myasthenia gravis, asthma, and alpha-thalassemia trait who returns for routine prenatal care following her prior visit for dyspnea and fundal height concerns.
She reports that she has been feeling generally well but mentions a mild cold-like illness about two weeks ago with low-grade fever, fatigue, and nasal congestion that resolved on its own.
The patient denies any recent travel or known exposures to infectious illnesses.
She notes that several of the children in her class have recently had viral infections.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
She works as a preschool teacher.
During this visit, a routine ultrasound is performed, and the fetus is noted to have ascites, skin edema, and a small pericardial effusion.
A follow-up doppler ultrasound shows elevated peak systolic velocity in the fetal middle cerebral artery.
Serologic testing is ordered to investigate the etiology of the fetal findings.

encounters.cc: Recent illness with low-grade fever, fatigue, and mild rash on cheeks; several students had similar symptoms last week

lines: Recent illness with low-grade fever, fatigue, and mild rash on cheeks; several students had similar symptoms last week
The patient is a 28-year-old female with myasthenia gravis, asthma, and alpha-thalassemia trait who returns following parvovirus B19 infection one month ago.
She reports low-grade fever, fatigue, and mild rash on her cheeks that she noticed a few days ago.
She works as an elementary school teacher and reports several of her students had similar symptoms last week.
She has had an uncomplicated pregnancy thus far.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, she has a faint erythematous rash on her cheeks with no other abnormalities.
The complete blood count is normal.
The fetal ultrasound reveals increased nuchal translucency, pericardial effusion, and ascites.
Her obstetrician orders a complete blood count and a fetal ultrasound due to her profession and symptoms.

encounters.cc: Decreased fetal movements over the past two days

lines: Decreased fetal movements over the past two days

The patient, a 28-year-old female with Myasthenia gravis on chronic immunosuppression who was evaluated earlier today in the outpatient obstetrics clinic, presents to the Emergency Department with decreased fetal movements over the past two days.
She reports no vaginal bleeding, leakage of fluid, or contractions.
Her first pregnancy was uneventful, and she delivered a healthy full-term infant.
She has had routine prenatal care.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 88 bpm, and temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F).
Ultrasound examination reveals a single fetus with skin edema and ascites.
There is no evidence of placental abruption or previa.
Fetal heart rate monitoring shows a baseline rate of 160 bpm with minimal variability and no accelerations.

encounters.cc: No fetal movements for the past 24 hours at 26 weeks gestation

lines: No fetal movements for the past 24 hours at 26 weeks gestation
The patient with Myasthenia gravis, Asthma, and Alpha-thalassemia trait returns reporting no fetal movements for 24 hours following recent viral illness and decreased fetal movements.
She is 26 weeks pregnant with her first child with uncomplicated pregnancy to date and regular prenatal care, denying vaginal bleeding, abdominal pain, fever, or trauma.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, her vital signs are stable,
Her abdomen is appropriately sized for gestational age, but no fetal heart tones are detected with Doppler ultrasound.
An obstetric ultrasound confirms intrauterine fetal demise with no cardiac activity.
The patient is understandably distressed and requests some time to process the information before making any decisions about management.

encounters.cc: One-month history of fatigue, easy bruising, and frequent nosebleeds

lines: One-month history of fatigue, easy bruising, and frequent nosebleeds

The patient is a 28-year-old female with Myasthenia gravis, Asthma, and Alpha-thalassemia trait, with a history of intrauterine fetal demise secondary to Parvovirus B19 infection six months prior, who presents to Hematology & Oncology.
She reports a recent upper respiratory tract infection that resolved two weeks ago.
She denies any significant past medical history.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, she appears pale and has scattered petechiae on her lower extremities.
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly is noted.
- White blood cell count: 2.1 x 10^9/L (Normal: 4-11 x 10^9/L)
- Peripheral blood smear: No abnormal cells or schistocytes
A bone marrow biopsy is performed, which shows profound hypocellularity with fatty infiltration.

encounters.cc: Five-day history of cough and mild shortness of breath following low-grade fever and malaise

lines: Five-day history of cough and mild shortness of breath following low-grade fever and malaise
The patient with alpha-thalassemia and prior Parvovirus B19 infection returns for follow-up.
She reports a low-grade fever and malaise that started a week ago, which has since resolved.
She denies any chest pain, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Her past medical history is significant for asthma.
She uses an albuterol inhaler as needed. She does not take any other medications.
- Pyridostigmine 60 mg PO every 4 to 6 hours
She has no known drug allergies
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On physical examination, her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respiratory rate is 20/min.
Oxygen saturation on room air is 97%.
Lung auscultation reveals scattered wheezes bilaterally, but no rales or rhonchi.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.
A chest radiograph shows no evidence of pneumonia or other abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Progressive difficulty breathing and swallowing over the past 2 days following respiratory infection

lines: Progressive difficulty breathing and swallowing over the past 2 days following respiratory infection
The patient with known myasthenia gravis presents following telehealth evaluation earlier today.
She reports that her symptoms have progressively worsened over the past 2 days.
She mentions that she had a respiratory tract infection last week but did not seek medical attention.
Her medical history is significant for myasthenia gravis, which was diagnosed 3 years ago.
She has been on pyridostigmine and prednisone.
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs inhaled PRN for shortness of breath
- One healthy child (age 2) from prior uncomplicated pregnancy
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Elementary school teacher.
On examination, she has bilateral ptosis and diplopia.
Her speech is nasal, and she is drooling.
Neck flexor muscle strength is 3/5, and respiratory examination reveals shallow breathing with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute.
Arterial blood gas shows a pH of 7.32, PaCO2 of 50 mmHg, PaO2 of 60 mmHg, and bicarbonate of 24 mEq/L.
